summary:
COSMOS – MISSION CONTROL

COSMOS is an educational game where players design, launch and manage space missions. Choose Lunar, Mars, Asteroid, Earth Observation, Deep Space or Custom missions, each with distance, delta-v, sunlight, communication and budget needs.

Build a spacecraft by choosing its body, power source, batteries, antenna, propulsion, thermal protection, navigation, landing system and scientific instruments. Each choice affects mass, cost, power and capability. Adjust fuel and select a launch vehicle: Sparrow-1, Kestrel-M, Atlas Ridge or Titan Crown.

Plan the mission, select scientific objectives, set instrument duty cycles and communication windows, and check design limits. The simulation covers countdown, liftoff, cruise, orbital insertion or descent, experiments, data transmission and completion. A dashboard tracks fuel, battery, power, distance, communication and spacecraft health.

Players handle solar-array, communication, navigation, thermal, power, fuel and instrument failures. Decisions affect outcomes. Instruments investigate minerals, atmospheres, asteroids, climate, radiation and ice.

A final report scores mission success, science, budget, mass, power, emergency response and communication out of 100. It suggests improvements, so players can redesign and try again.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, COSMOS runs in a browser with a tutorial and save/resume. It teaches engineering trade-offs, systems thinking and resource management.
details: COSMOS – MISSION CONTROL is an educational game where players design, launch and manage simulated missions to the Moon, Mars, asteroids, Earth and deep space. Players choose a mission, build a spacecraft and balance mass, cost, fuel, power, propulsion, communication and scientific instruments. They select a launch vehicle, set science objectives, plan instrument activity and communication windows, then simulate launch, cruise, orbital insertion or descent, experiments and data transmission. A dashboard tracks fuel, battery, power, distance, communication and spacecraft health. Simulated emergencies test decision-making. A final report scores mission success, science, budget, mass, power, emergency response and communication, and recommends improvements. The game makes space-engineering concepts easier to explore through hands-on experimentation. It aims to build curiosity about space science and STEM while developing systems thinking, resource management and problem-solving. Its creative approach combines spacecraft design, mission planning, live operations, unexpected events and performance feedback. Design factors include mission requirements, limited resources, engineering trade-offs, reliability and scientific goals. Developed with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, it runs in a browser with a responsive interface, tutorial and save/resume feature. Its calculations and outcomes are simplified educational simulations, not professional engineering predictions.
